Detailed Description

plugin that creates an icon.

this is an "advanced" icon-factory that uses the icon_set_state() method to modify icons dynamically rather than to precompute the states. this is the suggested procedure.

visually, this will create icons that look a bit like those used by the nautilus file-manager: text-labels appear below the icon-image; when selected, the text-label is underlaid with a grey box with filed off corners.

long text-labels are wrapped; for each wrap, the text-size is decreased by one.

icons may be overlaid with automatic "emblems" indicating that an item might not be accessible or writable by the current user. in the default theme, this is indicated by the stop-sign and eye of horus, respectively.

icons may be overlaid with additional textual information; at this time, the number of items contained in a folder is superimposed over the folder's icon. if the exact number of items is not known, an estimate is made ("123+" rather than "4711"). this estimate coincides with the number of folders contained in the folder (normally the number of hardlinks-2).

items that are symlinks are "ghosted"; they appear translucent.

items that evidence's thumbnailer was able to generate previews for will be show a preview in lieu of a datafile-icon.

the factory installs a variety of properties; see below. these properties can be set in themes, or from the typebuffer, e.g. 'icontextcolour ff00ff

int icon_set_state (  icon_list *  il,
icon *  icon,
icon_state  s
) 
 

change an icon's state.

an icon-factory may create elements for all states when the icon is first created; in this case, icon_set_state() needs not be provided. using icon_set_state() does however allow for more flexibility (and reduced use of memory) by creating the desired elements "on the fly."

Returns:
TRUE if evas_icon_set_state() wrapper show show/hide icon-elements based on their states after calling this, FALSE otherwise. (usually FALSE)
Parameters:
il - the icon-list
icon - the icon in question
s - the desired state
